answer: Registration needs a proof of work of 20 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the willow. The identity then has to pass a kernel challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next karst. Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. Mass registration costs one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent pays only once. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
